concepts.def: Reaction in plants that uses light energy to make glucose: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
Green pigment in chloroplasts that absorbs light energy.
Photosynthesis takes in energy from light.
The factor (light, CO₂, temperature) currently restricting rate of photosynthesis.
Respiration, stored as starch, used to make cellulose, proteins (with nitrate), fats.
Rate increases until enzymes denature, usually above ~40°C.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Photosynthesis & Plants — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Photosynthesis & Plants brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Photosynthesis & Plants.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a limiting factor for photosynthesis?

numericals.q: If photosynthesis rate doubles when light doubles up to 50%, what is the rate at 25% light if it is 8 units at 50% light?

free_texts.q: What green pigment absorbs light for photosynthesis?
